s.t: See where the trains are right now. Tap one to find out where it's going and when it gets to each stop.
Train data is provided by MassDOT, MBTA, Amtrak, MTA, Metra, NJ Transit, CTrail, and MARC. RailroadRadar is not responsible for inaccuracies.
Choose what the map shows, set up alerts, and manage your account.
Pick what to load for a faster start. You can change this anytime in Settings.
Get a notification when your upcoming MBTA trip's train is boarding on its track. Works in desktop browsers and the Home Screen app, including when RailroadRadar is closed.
On iPhone: open RailroadRadar from the Home Screen icon (not Safari), then turn these on. Safari itself cannot receive alerts after you leave the page.
You can disable notifications in RailroadRadar settings and in your browser or operating-system permission controls.
See every scheduled Commuter Rail train on a line for the day you pick, or plan a trip on Commuter Rail and the subway.
See every scheduled Commuter Rail train on a line for the day you pick, or plan a trip on Commuter Rail and the subway.
Keep track of the trains you ride. Save each trip and look back on everywhere you've been.
Log trains, keep your miles, and share trips with a public MyTrips page.
Log a ride to start your miles and see routes on the map.
Miles are approximate station-to-station estimates.
Share a trip image or your public profile
Share a public page with your name, photo, and trip log. Email stays private.
Set a username in Account settings first.
Share a live trip with your family and friends using the share button on train pop-ups!
Going live asks for your location and shares it on the map for up to 5 hours.
A share ends when you stop it or after 5 hours at most; when it ends we delete it, and any copy left behind after it expires is removed in our next cleanup.
Sign in to report locomotives, log your trips, and choose which railroads you follow.
You may browse the public map without an account. Submitting reports and saving watch lists requires Google sign-in.
You choose how your name appears on reports: first initial, full Google display name, a custom label, or "Anonymous." Your email and raw Google name are not shown on the public map.
Share a public page with your name, photo, and trip log. Email stays private.

You may delete your account from the account menu. Deleting removes your sign-in account, account and settings records, public profile and username, trip logs, any live location share, pending reports, and your press-release comments.

Public train reports you already submitted stay on trains with the label they were posted under, and the admin-only audit copy of your reports and any ban or appeal records are kept for moderation; email railroadradar@gmail.com and we will delete or anonymize those on request where we can.
Sign in with Google to pair locomotives to live trains and share what you see.
Signed-in users can pair locomotives or special units to live or scheduled trains and add comments.
No train reports this week yet. Report a consist to get on the board.
Station audio announcements. Nothing is spoken until you press Start.
Press Start or Test sound once to unlock audio.
See which trips each MBTA Commuter Rail vehicle ran over the last 4 days. Search by the vehicle ID the MBTA gives each train.
Restaurants, stores, and other businesses that are easy to reach by public transit, train-themed, or welcoming to train fans.

Google provides your account identifier, email address, display name, and profile photo (if your Google account includes one). We collect your email so we can moderate reports and reach you about your account.
We do not sell your personal information. We do not use your reports or account data to build advertising profiles or to show third-party ads.
We do not require location to use the map; it is needed only to log a new special move, which starts a live location share.
Email us to request access to, correction of, or deletion of personal information we hold about you, including a copy of your data (we do not yet offer a self-service export).
When you first visit the map, a banner asks about cookies. You can agree, decline, or choose Customize to decide about analytics yourself. Analytics stays off unless you agree to it.
Analytics stays off unless you turn it on. You can change this any time with Cookie Settings at the bottom of the page.

Stay off tracks and railroad property. Walking on or along tracks, or going into yards, rights-of-way, bridges, or tunnels without permission, is trespassing. It is against the law, and it can kill you.
Cross only at marked crossings. Obey all signals, gates, bells, and signs. Never go around or under a lowered gate.
On platforms, stay back from the edge. Stand behind the yellow line or edge markings, and follow posted rules and railroad staff.
Watch and take photos only from places you are allowed to be, such as public sidewalks, roads, parks, and the public areas of stations.
Never rely on RailroadRadar for a safety decision.
Emergencies: call 911.

A problem at a railroad crossing (for example, a vehicle stuck on the tracks, or a gate or signal that isn't working): if anyone is on the tracks, get them off and well away first. Then call the railroad's emergency number on the blue-and-white Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign at the crossing, and give the crossing number shown on the sign.
MBTA Transit Police: 617-222-1212, or text 617-600-0683
Amtrak Police: 800-331-0008, or text APD11 (27311)
MTA Police (Metro-North and the Long Island Rail Road): 888-682-9117 for emergencies, or 212-878-1001
NJ TRANSIT Police: 973-378-6565 or 800-242-0236, or text NJTPD (65873)
Metra Police: 312-322-2800, or 312-322-2999 for non-emergencies
In the U.S., call or text 988 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. In Canada, call or text 9-8-8.
If you see something on RailroadRadar that breaks these rules, email us at railroadradar@gmail.com.
